name: CHEM_V
field_tax_subject_notes:
Students without BC Secondary School Chemistry 12 or equivalent are required to take the UBC Chemistry Basic Skills Test. Students receiving a satisfactory score on this Test take CHEM_V 111. With permission of the department head, students not receiving a satisfactory score on this Test take CHEM_V 100. Students with credit for CHEM_V 100 may take CHEM_V 121. Students with BC Secondary School Chemistry 12 or equivalent must take CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 141 or CHEM_V 154. CHEM_V 100 and CHEM_V 111 are not open to students with credit for Chemistry 12. CHEM_V 141 is suggested for students with an academic interest in lab-focused sciences such as Chemistry, Biochemistry, or similar subjects. Students with credit for CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 121 or CHEM_V 141 may take CHEM_V 123, a requirement for many Science programs. The following courses are for students in the Faculty of Applied Science: CHEM_V 154, CHEM_V 250, CHEM_V 251, CHEM_V 260. The Department lists courses that comprise the individual lecture and laboratory components for courses that contain both. The course(s) that may substitute are: """" CHEM_V 111 (4) = CHEM_V 110 (3) and CHEM_V 115 (1) """" CHEM_V 121 (4) = CHEM_V 120 (3) and CHEM_V 115 (1) """" CHEM_V 123 (4) = CHEM_V 130 (3) and CHEM_V 135 (1) """" CHEM_V 203 (4) = CHEM_V 223 (3) and CHEM_V 225 (1) """" CHEM_V 211 (4) = CHEM_V 210 (3) and CHEM_V 215 (1)

Transfer students with 4 credits of CHEM 1st will be deemed to have satisfied the requirement of CHEM_V 121. Transfer students with 8 credits of CHEM 1st will be deemed to have satisfied both the CHEM_V 121 and CHEM_V 123 requirements.

name: CPSC_V
field_tax_subject_notes: The Department of Computer Science offers several options in first year: CPSC_V 110 is for students pursuing Computer Science specializations or who plan to take CPSC_V 210. CPSC_V 103 targets students desiring an introduction to computing and programming, but with no plans to take further Computer Science courses. CPSC_V 100 targets students desiring a general introduction to computational thinking with little programming. Consult https://www.cs.ubc.ca/students/undergrad/courses/choose-your-first-course for more information. Students who have credit for or exemption from APSC_V 160, CPSC_V 107 or CPSC_V 110 may not take CPSC_V 100 or CPSC_V 103. Students with other computer science transfer credit must consult the department. Students currently registered in CPSC_V 110 or with Computer Science credit from another institution may not take APSC_V 160 for credit. Students with sufficient background in the concepts presented in CPSC_V 110 and an advisor's approval are encouraged to challenge CPSC_V 110 for credit by taking an examination. Additional fees are charged for some courses. For more information students are advised to contact the Department of Computer Science or visit its undergraduate website: http://www.cs.ubc.ca/students/undergrad). For information on credit exclusion between CPSC_V and other courses, please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List.

name: PHYS_V
field_tax_subject_notes:
Science students with BC Secondary School Physics 11, but not Physics 12, are required to take PHYS_V 100. PHYS_V 100 is intended primarily for students who have completed only Physics 11 or its equivalent. Credit will not be given for PHYS_V 100 to students with credit for Physics 12 unless they took AP, IB, or A-level Physics and were offered advanced credit for PHYS_V 100. Most Science degree specializations require at least one or two terms of physics beyond Physics 12 or PHYS_V 100. Science One is considered to include two terms of physics. Credit will be given for only one of PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107 and for only one of PHYS_V 102, PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118. Many other PHYS_V courses are credit-excluded with each other, or with courses in other departments. Students should consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List: https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists.

Transfer students with 3 credits of PHYS 1st will be deemed to have satisfied all PHYS_V 101, 106, 107, all 131 requirements. Transfer students with 6 credits of PHYS 1st will be deemed to have satisfied all PHYS_V 101, 106, 107, 131 and PHYS_V 108 or 118 requirements. Students who have completed a physics laboratory experience with their transfer credit can apply for an exemption for PHYS_V 119 through the Department of Physics and Astronomy (https://phas.ubc.ca/students/contact-us).
